title: FDA approves Roche's Gazyva as first drug for primary membranous nephropathy
summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Nov. 13, 2026, approved Genentech's Gazyva (obinutuzumab) to induce remission of proteinuria in adults with primary membranous nephropathy who are at risk of disease progression, making the Roche unit's anti-CD20 antibody the first drug cleared in the United States specifically for the rare autoimmune kidney disease. title: Boy with rare condition amazes doctors after world-first gene therapy | BBC News | Project Alive
summary: Three-year-old Oliver Chu has astounded doctors with his progress after becoming the first person in the world with his devastating disease to receive a ground-breaking gene therapy. "Every time we talk about it, I want to cry because it's just so amazing," says the boy’s mother, Jingru. He has a rare, inherited condition called Hunter syndrome - or MPSII - which causes progressive damage to the body and brain. In the most severe cases, patients with the disease usually die before the age of 20.

summary: Intellia Therapeutics reported on November 12 that one infusion of its CRISPR gene-editing therapy lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z) has kept hereditary angioedema (HAE) attack rates 89% below patients' own baselines for up to four years, and that every patient on the 50 mg dose was free of long-term preventive drugs at the data cutoffs.
